To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a single injection of suramin (20 mg/kg) followed 3-4 days later by one of a range of 2-substitute 5-nitromidazoles given either as a single treatment (10 mg/kg) or a course of daily treatments (10 mg/kg/day for 3-5 days), is an effective treatment for chronic infections of T. brucei with central nervous system (CNS) involvement, which are normally resistant to conventional chemotherapy.
5-nitromidazole compounds can eliminateTrypanosoma from the central nervous sytem of mice and may be of value in the treatment of human sleeping sickness.

the treatment of chronic infections withTrypanosoma (Trypanozoon) brucei in mice, which relapse after standard chemotherapy because infective parasites in the brain escape drug action and are able to re-establish a parasitemia, is prevented by a 2- substituted 5-nitromidazole, which kills trypanosomes in both the peripheral blood and the central nervous system, even when administered at a low dose level.

the treatment ofTrypanosomabrucei infections, particularly in those animals with central nervous system (CNS) involvement, which are normally not cured by conventional chemotherapy.
the use of the 5-nitr0imidazoles as single agents in the treatment of Trypanosoma brucel infections.
the use of 2-alkyl-5-nitro-1H-imidazoles as potential drugs for the treatment of human sleeping sickness, caused by Trypanosoma brucie.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a single dose of suramin followed 72 h later by a 5-nitrofuryl 2-imidazole (L634,549) is an effective treatment againstTrypanosoma rhodesiense andTrypanosoma gambiense infections.
a combination of suramin followed by 5-nitromidazoles is the most effective and safe treatment for chronic murineTryp. brucei infections.

the use of the 5-ni-troimidazoles is not only effective against trypanosomes in blood but that it is also effective against trypanosomiasis in the central nervous system, and that this effect is independent of the presence of suramin in the treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 2-substituents on the 5-nirroimidazoles are responsible for the activity against trypanosomes in mice and the 4- or 6-substituents are responsible for activity in rats and humans.
, in mice with chronic infections ofT. b. brucei, 1×20mg/kg suramin, given intraperitonally, is a useful adjunct to 5-nitrofuran treatment.
the 5-nitoimidazoles, given in combination with suramin, are effective againstTrypanosoma rhodesiense andT. b. gambiense in mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 5-nitoimidazole compounds are effective in the treatment of central nervous system trypanosomiasis, but they are not as potent as the arsenicals.
the 5-nitoimidazoles can cure trypanosomes from mice with CNS involvement.
